title: 276. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Logarithmic Graph Monotonicity by Base
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Monotonicity of Logarithmic Functions by Base
questions.learningObjective: Identify whether a logarithmic function is increasing or decreasing from its base.
questions.question: Which function is increasing on its domain?
questions.explanation: For \(y=\log_b x\), the function is increasing when \(b>1\) and decreasing when \(0<b<1\). Since \(4>1\), the function \(y=\log_4 x\) is increasing. Since \(0.4<1\), the function \(y=\log_{0.4} x\) is decreasing. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the base with the number \(1\).

questions.concept: Monotonicity of Logarithmic Functions by Base
questions.learningObjective: Identify whether a logarithmic function is increasing or decreasing from its base.
questions.question: Which function is decreasing on its domain?
questions.explanation: For \(y=\log_b x\), the function is decreasing when \(0<b<1\). Since \(\frac{1}{7}\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), the function \(y=\log_{\frac{1}{7}} x\) is decreasing. Since \(7>1\), \(y=\log_7 x\) is increasing. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: A base between \(0\) and \(1\) gives a decreasing logarithmic function.

questions.concept: Graph Shape of Logarithmic Functions with Base Between \(0\) and \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Determine the monotonic behavior of \(y=\log_b x\) when \(0<b<1\).
questions.question: For \(y=\log_b x\) with \(0<b<1\), which statement describes the graph on its domain?
questions.explanation: When the base \(b\) satisfies \(0<b<1\), the logarithmic function \(y=\log_b x\) is decreasing on \((0,\infty)\). As \(x\) increases, the output decreases. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the effect of the base being less than \(1\) on the direction of the logarithmic graph.

questions.concept: Choosing a Base for an Increasing Logarithmic Function
questions.learningObjective: Select a base that makes \(y=\log_b x\) increasing.
questions.question: Which base makes \(y=\log_b x\) an increasing function?
questions.explanation: The logarithmic function \(y=\log_b x\) is increasing when \(b>1\). Since \(3>1\), the base \(b=3\) makes the function increasing. The base \(b=\frac{1}{3}\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), which would make the function decreasing. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: An increasing logarithmic function requires a base greater than \(1\).

questions.concept: Comparing Logarithmic Values with Different Bases
questions.learningObjective: Compare two logarithmic values for \(x>1\) when both bases are greater than \(1\).
questions.question: For \(x>1\), which value is greater?
questions.explanation:
For \(x>1\), we have \(\ln x>0\). Using the change-of-base formula,
\[
\log_2 x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln 2},\qquad \log_5 x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln 5}
\]
Since \(0<\ln 2<\ln 5\), dividing the positive number \(\ln x\) by the smaller denominator \(\ln 2\) gives a larger result. Therefore \(\log_2 x>\log_5 x\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Use the change-of-base formula and compare the denominators.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two logarithmic values for \(x>1\) when both bases are between \(0\) and \(1\).
questions.question: Let \(0<a<b<1\) and \(x>1\). Which value is smaller?
questions.explanation:
Using the change-of-base formula,
\[
\log_a x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln a},\qquad \log_b x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln b}
\]
Since \(x>1\), \(\ln x>0\). Since \(0<a<b<1\), we have \(\ln a<\ln b<0\). Therefore
\[
\frac{\ln x}{\ln b}<\frac{\ln x}{\ln a}
\]
so \(\log_b x<\log_a x\). Hence \(\log_b x\) is smaller, and option B is correct.
questions.hint: Both functions are decreasing; compare the sizes of the negative logarithms of the bases.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the monotonic behavior of \(y=\log_{10} x\).
questions.question: Which statement is correct for \(y=\log_{10} x\) on its domain?
questions.explanation: The base is \(10\), which is greater than \(1\). Therefore the logarithmic function \(y=\log_{10} x\) is increasing on \((0,\infty)\). As \(x\) increases, the output also increases. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether the base is greater than \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Select the logarithmic function that is decreasing on its domain.
questions.question: Which function is decreasing on its domain?
questions.explanation: For \(y=\log_b x\), the function is decreasing when \(0<b<1\). Since \(0.3\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), \(y=\log_{0.3} x\) is decreasing. Since \(3>1\), \(y=\log_3 x\) is increasing. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: A base less than \(1\) produces a decreasing logarithmic graph.

questions.learningObjective: Select the logarithmic function that is increasing on its domain.
questions.question: Which function is increasing on its domain?
questions.explanation: For \(y=\log_b x\), the function is increasing when \(b>1\). Since \(1.1>1\), \(y=\log_{1.1} x\) is increasing. Since \(0.9\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), \(y=\log_{0.9} x\) is decreasing. Therefore option B is correct.

questions.concept: Comparing Logarithmic Values with a Base Between \(0\) and \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Use the decreasing behavior of \(y=\log_b x\) for \(0<b<1\) to compare two logarithmic values.
questions.question: Which value is larger?
questions.explanation: Since \(0<\frac{1}{2}<1\), the function \(y=\log_{\frac{1}{2}} x\) is decreasing on \((0,\infty)\), so a larger input gives a smaller output. Because \(3<5\), we have \(\log_{\frac{1}{2}} 3>\log_{\frac{1}{2}} 5\). Indeed, \(\log_{\frac{1}{2}} 3\approx -1.585\) and \(\log_{\frac{1}{2}} 5\approx -2.322\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Decide whether \(y=\log_{\frac{1}{2}} x\) is increasing or decreasing, then compare the inputs \(3\) and \(5\).
